baseline.authority: docs/design/PO_DECISION_RECORD_2026_09_14_DEVICE_ADD_ENTRY_PEER_FOLLOW_AND_CREDENTIAL_STORE.md (FROZEN, 2026-09-14), section CS-1, whose credential_store schema is implemented verbatim by ui2/service/src/main/resources/db/migration/V11__credential_store.sql. That migration carries the load-bearing rule: chk_credentials_passphrase_only_for_private_key -- a credential row may hold a non-null encrypted_passphrase only when kind = 'ssh_private_key'. The constraint is correct and stays exactly as written; this movement is about what happens before a write reaches it, not about the rule itself.
baseline.engineering: The failing update was atomic: the audited transaction boundary rolled back on the constraint violation, so the credential's stored secret and secret_set_at were unchanged by the failed attempt (measured directly against the row afterwards). No credential material was lost or corrupted by this defect; the defect is entirely in what the operator could attempt and how the failure was reported.
baseline.observed: Replacing a credential's secret through the UI returned 'Internal Server Error' with no further detail. Measured cause, from the ui2-service log: a raw PSQLException from the check constraint above, because ReplaceSecretDialog in CredentialsPanel.tsx always renders a 'Passphrase (optional)' field and always sends whatever it holds, regardless of the credential's own kind. The credential being replaced was kind ssh_password, for which the constraint forbids any passphrase at all. CreateCredentialDialog in the same file already gates its own passphrase field on kind === 'ssh_private_key'; ReplaceSecretDialog was never given the kind to gate on.
